story.title: manifest lifts a CI test command out of its working directory
story.source_text: evidence.py manifest reports a test command that does not run at the repo root. Steps to reproduce: 1. python3 story-refinery/scripts/evidence.py manifest --config story-refinery/evals/self-run/refinery.yaml on skills@eeb5595 (Linux, Python 3.11). 2. Read the summary line. Expected: a test command that runs from the repo root, or none, with the file it came from. Actual: `test=python -m pytest tests/ -q -rs`, lifted from .github/workflows/terrain-architect.yml, whose `defaults.run.working-directory` is terrain-architect/reference-impl; there is no tests/ at the root, so the command fails with 'no tests ran' and the source file is not shown. Impact: every monorepo with per-package CI; the wrong command lands in agent briefs as a done_when and becomes a false completion gate. Workaround: none short of editing the manifest by hand.
story.summary_human: The manifest scanner reads `run:` lines out of CI workflows but ignores `defaults.run.working-directory`, so a command that only runs inside terrain-architect/reference-impl is presented as the repo's test command and lands in briefs as a done_when that fails at the root. Fix: honour the workflow default and step-level working-directory by prefixing `cd <dir> &&`, and print the source file next to each command. Failing test first, then the fix.
story.technical_notes_human: Root cause (D1): `detect_commands` (`story-refinery/scripts/evidence.py:94`) matches `run:`/`script:` lines (l.108) and records the first test-looking one via `put` (l.98), never reading `defaults.run.working-directory` or a step's `working-directory:`. The workflow sets the default at `.github/workflows/terrain-architect.yml:25` and the command at l.59. `command_sources` already records the file; the summary print at l.399 just does not show it. The manifest is sha-keyed, so a fixed scanner only takes effect on a rebuild - compatibility note in the handover. No YAML parser is available (stdlib only, `_yaml.py` is a subset reader) - the fix tracks the two keys with the same line-regex style as the existing loop.

decisions.question: Root cause: why does a sub-project's command surface as the repo's?

options.label: The regex only sees `run:` lines and has no notion of working directory
options.tradeoff: the cause; fix is local to detect_commands

options.label: The manifest schema cannot express a cwd
options.tradeoff: true but not the cause - the command string can carry `cd dir &&`

decisions.chosen: The regex only sees `run:` lines and has no notion of working directory
decisions.rationale: evidence.py:104-108 reads lines in isolation; the workflow's default at terrain-architect.yml:25 is never read. Five whys stop here: this is the first cause we own and can fix.

decisions.question: Carry the directory in the command string, or as a separate manifest field?

options.label: `cd <dir> && <command>` in the string
options.tradeoff: no schema change; every consumer that runs the string gets it right

options.label: a `cwd` field per command
options.tradeoff: cleaner data; every consumer must be updated, and briefs copy the string

decisions.rationale: Briefs and done_when copy the string verbatim; a separate field would be dropped on the way.

findings.claim: A workflow-level default is under `defaults:` → `run:` → `working-directory:`, three lines deep; the loop's `run:` regex will match the `run:` line under `defaults:` as a command with empty text.
findings.failure: `put` is never called for empty text (`if key not in cmds and value`), so nothing breaks - but an implementer reading the regex may special-case it and lose the default.
findings.resolution: Harmless today by the `and value` guard at evidence.py:99; noted in S2's read_first so it is not 'fixed'.

findings.claim: The boundary case names `(pyproject.toml)` but detect_commands records the source of an inferred python command as the string 'python project', not a filename.
findings.failure: S1's third check expects a filename and fails after S2 for the wrong reason.
findings.resolution: example now expects `(python project)`, the source string the code already records.

findings.claim: The first done_when grepped for lines that S1 must name exactly; the objective did not fix the names.
findings.failure: An implementer names the checks differently and the grep counts 0.
findings.resolution: the three names are in S1's objective verbatim and the grep counts them.
